incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 6, 8, 19 (Articles of Incorporation, registered office, corporate powers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA; shares may be issued without par value for any lawful consideration and no escrow account requirement applies to a standard commercial federal corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED: ONE — The Articles of Incorporation filed with Corporations Canada under the Canada Business Corporations Act and the resulting Certificate of Incorporation are hereby approved and accepted. TWO — The Corporation shall issue 1,000 Class A common shares to its sole subscriber for CAD 1.00, fully paid and non-assessable; the subscription funds shall be deposited to the corporate account. THREE — The registered office of the Corporation is established at 100 King Street West, Suite 5600, Toronto, Ontario as stated in the Articles of Incorporation. FOUR — The inaugural directors are confirmed and the officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary. FIVE — By-Law No. 1 governing the conduct of corporate affairs is adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada via accredited NUANS search houses
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) request for the proposed corporate name combined with vertical micro-drama production descriptors; review the preliminary search report for conflicts; file a Name Reservation Request online to reserve the approved name for 90 days; proceed to Articles drafting only upon name approval.
required_dossiers: Statement of directors' authorization for name request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a conflicting name is flagged, submit an alternate NUANS search or file the reservation with an additional distinctive word; a written consent letter from the conflict holder may be used to cure the conflict.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation with Corporations Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Online Filing Portal (Virtual Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 4001 online: proposed name, registered office address (must be a Canadian physical address), share classes (Class A common voting, Class B non-voting as needed), number of directors and first directors' names with addresses; pay the CAD 200 fee by credit card; the electronic Certificate of Incorporation is issued upon approval by a Corporations Canada analyst.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by the analyst, correct the stated deficiency and resubmit online within 30 days; the filing fee is retained and applied to the resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Organizational By-Laws, Officer Appointments and Registered Office Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (corporate action)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or obtain written resolutions; adopt By-Law No. 1 governing corporate affairs, appoint the officers named in the First Board Resolution, ratify the registered office address, approve the bank account resolution, and maintain minutes in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable, proceed by unanimous written resolution in lieu of a meeting pursuant to section 117 of the CBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Extra-Provincial Registration in the Operating Province
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial registry — e.g., Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (ServiceOntario) or the equivalent registry of the province of operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an Application for Extra-Provincial Registration with the applicable provincial registry, naming the federal corporation, confirming the registered head office and principal place of business in the province, and appointing a provincial attorney for service; pay the provincial filing fee (e.g., CAD 210 for Ontario).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, correct the provincial name registration discrepancy (usually a NUANS listing issue) and refile; request a Federal Certificate of Status to evidence good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Tax Registration, Corporate Minute Book, and Business Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via Business Registration Online; financial institution of choice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a Business Number (BN) and program accounts (e.g., GST/HST, payroll) through CRA Business Registration Online; prepare the minute book with articles, by-laws, share certificates and share register; provide the signing officers and corporate documents to the bank to open the operating account into which the share subscription funds are deposited.
required_dossiers: Form RC1 — Request for a Business Number
Minute book records and share subscription evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN registration is delayed, contact the CRA Business Window; if bank account opening is delayed, obtain a certified Certificate of Status from Corporations Canada to verify corporate existence and good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no federal production licence; only sectoral registration touchpoint is the CRTC Basic Registration for Online Undertakings
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating licence required for vertical micro-drama production or streaming distribution under federal Canadian law; CRTC Basic Registration may apply to the streaming undertaking generating Canadian revenue

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office, digital post-production and streaming activities are not listed in the Physical Activities Regulations under the Impact Assessment Act, 2019
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge. General compliance with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 for VOC emissions (cleaning agents, set paints) and municipal sewer by-laws (e.g., BOD 300 mg/L), with proper disposal of electronic waste under provincial extended producer responsibility regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: municipal fire marshal inspection certificate under the National Fire Code of Canada. Occupational: provincial occupational health and safety (e.g., Ontario OHSA) workplace inspection clearance, plus building and electrical permits for studio fit-out and set lighting installations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - My Business Account portal and GST/HST NETFILE
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity doing business in Canada must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA, which serves as the statutory TIN. Apply online through Business Registration Online or by filing Form RC1, requesting the GST/HST program account (RC). Registration is mandatory when taxable supplies made in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in the last four consecutive calendar quarters; non-resident suppliers of digital services may use the simplified GST/HST registration. The same BN is used for corporate income tax, payroll, and GST/HST; non-resident corporations may appoint a Canadian tax representative under section 273 of the Excise Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide U.S.-style check-the-box elections; corporate status is determined under the Canada Business Corporations Act and income tax law. Relevant domestic elections include: s. 85 rollover (tax-deferred transfer of property on incorporation/reorganization), s. 89(4) paid-up capital election, s. 95 foreign affiliate deemed-dividend election, and anti-hybrid mismatch conformity elections under ss. 18.4-18.5 and 20.5 of the Income Tax Act. For GST/HST, a registrant may elect under s. 156 to combine branches or use the quick method if the entity's taxable supplies (including those of associates) are no greater than CAD 400,000 in a fiscal year.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) - a value-added tax system; provincial retail sales taxes (PST/QST) apply in non-HST provinces
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Canada in any single calendar quarter or over the last four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold); the threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of streaming and digital services based on worldwide and Canadian supply volumes, without requiring physical presence.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no federal real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, XML clearance, or digital stamping mandate. GST/HST registrants may provide paper or PDF invoices, although electronic invoices and PDFs are valid. Registrants whose taxable supplies exceed CAD 1 million in a fiscal year must file GST/HST returns electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or My Business Account. No API-based tax authority clearance is required, but CRA can request supplier data in XML, CSV, or Excel during audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under s. 145 of the Excise Tax Act to: (i) supplies of goods that are exported by the supplier (documented export to a non-resident); (ii) supplies of services performed wholly outside Canada (or in Canada directly in respect of exported movable property) to a non-resident recipient; and (iii) supplies of intangible personal property, including streaming licences, copyright, and digital content, to a non-resident where all consideration is reasonably attributable to the enjoyment of the property outside Canada. For the vertical micro-drama business, sales of distribution rights to non-resident platforms and download sublicences are zero-rated where the geographic exploitation is confined to territories outside Canada; direct supplies to Canadian subscribers through app stores are taxable at 5% GST (or HST in participating provinces).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) record
Commercial invoice stating zero-rating under s. 145 of the Excise Tax Act
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill for physical media, or digital delivery logs / download reports for intangible content
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign currency bank statement evidencing receipt of export consideration
Distribution or licence agreement with non-resident counterparty defining territorial rights
Evidence of non-resident status (certificate of incorporation, permanent establishment analysis, or NR tax form)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated export beyond the four-year normal reassessment period if there is misrepresentation, negligence, fraud, or wilful default; denial of the zero-rating results in reapportioned GST/HST output tax plus interest under s. 280 of the Excise Tax Act. Gross negligence penalties of 25% of the net deficiency (ETA s. 285.1) and false-statement penalties under ITA s. 163.2 (50% of the misrepresented amount) may be imposed; criminal tax evasion can attract fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment for up to five years. Directors and officers remain jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/HST under ETA s. 323, and clawback risks are heightened in digital-export audits because CRA scrutinizes the geographic enjoyment of streaming rights and requires irrefutable non-resident evidence within the audit response period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the sole monetary and exchange-rate policy authority; residual foreign exchange powers rest with the Department of Finance Canada under the Currency Act. Canada maintains no separate Foreign Exchange Administration or exchange control licensing body; day-to-day enforcements of payment transparency are administered by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and by OSFI for bank prudential conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both current-account and capital-account transactions. The Canadian dollar is free-floating with no exchange controls, no conversion licensing, and no advance approval requirements for inward or outward flows. Profit remittance is subject only to standard fiscal gates: Part I corporate income tax on earned net income of CA_CORP at combined federal/provincial rates, a 25% Part XIII gross withholding tax on dividends, royalties, and certain interest paid to non-residents, and treaty-rate reductions (US typically 5%-15%, PRC typically 5%-10%, UK typically 5%-10% depending on ownership tier and treaty residency evidence). No exchange-control choke point exists on repatriation; practical hurdles are limited to FINTRAC threshold reporting on electronic funds transfers exceeding CAD 10,000, CRS/FATCA information reporting by the financial institution, and bank-level enhanced due diligence on flows from non-transparent jurisdictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion obligation exists in Canada. The Foreign Exchange Control Act regime was repealed in 1951, and neither the Bank of Canada Act nor the Currency Act imposes repatriation or conversion ratios. Export and streaming receipts (e.g., USD remittances from Apple App Store, Google Play, and Stripe) may be kept indefinitely in USD, held in a multi-currency operating account, or converted to CAD at market rates. Reporting duties are confined to FINTRAC obligations applicable to reporting financial institutions (incoming/outgoing EFTs exceeding CAD 10,000) and the CAD 10,000+ physical cross-border currency declaration; none of these restrict the exporter's retention or conversion rights.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as a settlement utility only; LOW-MEDIUM as a primary cash custodian. Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex can efficiently concentrate Apple/Google/Stripe payouts and disburse to foreign actors and post-production houses, but the following legal constraints apply: (i) a non-Canadian EMI carrying on money transmission or foreign exchange dealing in Canada must itself be registered as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and appoint a resident agent for service; (ii) EMI balances are not CDIC-insured except where passed through to a CDIC-member partner bank up to CAD 100,000; (iii) the corporate account holder must maintain accurate CRS/FATCA classification; (iv) if the corporation uses an EMI to pay out funds on behalf of third-party actors, it may cross the MSB de minimis threshold (CAD 1,000,000 in EFTs or 100 transmissions per calendar year) or be characterized as a third-party settlement organization; (v) recommended architecture is a Schedule I chartered bank as the principal cash-holding train, with a FINTRAC-registered EMI used solely for vendor payout rails and client-convenience conversion, never as the account of record for capital injection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires physical attendance by directors. PCMLTFA regulations and OSFI Guideline B-10 permit fully remote onboarding where video-identification, certified digital identity verification, and enhanced due diligence are applied consistent with FINTRAC Identity Verification Requirements. Standard Tier-1 onboarding for CA_CORP requires: (i) a virtual relationship interview of 15-30 minutes with at least one authorized director and, where non-resident controllers exist, a compliance call with the UBO; (ii) notarized or certified copies of passports and proof of address for all directors and 10%+ shareholders; (iii) certified Articles of Incorporation, Certificate of Compliance, current annual return, register of directors, and extra-provincial registration where applicable; (iv) a certified board resolution designating Canadian-based signing officers and approving account structure. Remote opening is viable for a 100% non-resident board provided central management and control in Canada is substantiated by documents and approved by the bank's financial crimes control unit; typical onboarding timeline is 10-15 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO concentration exceeding 25% from a high-risk or partially blocklisted jurisdiction, or a PEP-linked investor in the production financing chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Articles of Incorporation with Notice of Change filings; register of directors and 10%+ shareholders; UBO attestation with tax-residency and source-of-wealth declaration; DAO/business plan evidencing Canadian operational substance; licensed PEP and sanctions screening report; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; reference letters from existing Canadian counsel and prior bank; sworn board resolution confirming the equity or loan character of the funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket micro-transactions from Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and Stripe inconsistent with disclosed trade activity, creating suspicion of layering or shell operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly App Store Connect and Google Play settlement statements; Stripe Payout and Treasury account summaries; independent CPA reconciliation of subscriber analytics to settlement amounts; chain-of-title records for micro-drama IP (ISAN registration, copyright assignments, distribution licenses); documented refund and chargeback policy; PSP merchant agreements; FINTRAC transaction-log exports evidencing full traceability of each settlement batch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payments to related-party offshore post-production houses or actor-controlled SPVs, raising Part XIII withholding or disguised profit extraction concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed arm's-length production, licensing, and service agreements with economic-substance documentation; CRA Form NR301/NR302/NR303 waiver evidence and NR4 remittance proof; treaty residency certificates (US Form 6166, HK IRD Certificate of Residence, PRC tax residency certificate); OECD-aligned transfer-pricing comparability and EBITDA analysis; value-chain map demonstrating where IP development, filming, and risk actually reside; audited intercompany ledger reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipt of subscription funds from sanctioned entities or transit jurisdictions, or crypto/fan-token settlement rails contaminating the bank account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening records for all counterparties; counterparty beneficial-ownership certifications; payment-provider AVS and IP-geolocation block logs; board-adopted policy prohibiting crypto settlement (unless the entity separately registers as an MSB); FINTRAC STR reporting records; certified AML/CFT compliance program manual with a designated compliance officer; continuous periodic KYC refresh for actors, licensees, and distribution partners.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant circuit: (1) the subscribing non-resident or Canadian shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 from its primary bank to the CA_CORP Schedule I operating account with narration 'share subscription / paid-in capital' and SWIFT NPRM purpose code 'EQUI' (equity securities); producers must never use 'SERV', 'ROYT', or 'INTC' codes for equity capital, as a tainted narration can trigger Part XIII analysis; (2) the receiving bank applies standard CDD and obtains the corporate documents evidencing board approval of issuance, an allotment register entry, and, where shares are issued at a premium, a board-approved valuation; (3) settlement occurs within one to two business days through the CAD RTR/ACSS or correspondent Nostro rail; no CRA advance ruling or regulatory permit is required for inward equity; (4) FINTRAC EFT reporting for transfers above CAD 10,000 is the reporting institution's obligation, though the payer should pre-clear the purpose code with the receiving bank's financial crimes control unit; (5) if capital arrives as a shareholder or intercompany loan (purpose 'LOAN' or 'DEM'), a loan agreement on arm's-length terms, a section 212(1)(b) Part XIII withholding analysis, and treaty-rate election documentation (generally 0%-10% under US/PRC/UK treaties) must be prepared; (6) all inflows should be booked to the ledger with corresponding entries, CRS consent records, and source-of-funds files for audit readiness.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rail matrix: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for foreign actors, localization and dubbing houses, tax advisors, and co-producing distributors, with free-format narration replicating the underlying invoice reference and Part XIII remittance effected through CRA NR4 and tax remittance accounts; (ii) SWIFT MT700/MT710 documentary commercial letters of credit for high-value acquisition of distribution minimum guarantees, exclusive post-production packages, and equipment; (iii) domestic Canadian-dollar disbursements through Payments Canada ACSS (ACH) and Real-Time Rail for payroll and Canadian vendors; (iv) USD-denominated outflows routed through a dedicated USD operating account at the bank's New York or Federal correspondent to avoid double conversion; (v) Apple and Google USD settlements are swept into the USD master account, then either hedged via forward or converted at bank spot to fund CAD obligations; (vi) weekly benchmarking of FX rates against Bloomberg WM Close or bank flat-fee margin schedules to evidence arm's-length pricing; (vii) sanctions-scrubbed beneficiary accounts (OFAC, UNSC, EU, and comparable Canadian Autonomous Sanctions lists) as a condition precedent to every disbursement in excess of CAD 25,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC deliverable USD/CAD forward contracts (up to 24 months) under an ISDA 1992 Master Agreement or Canadian Derivatives Master Agreement, fully permitted given free convertibility and bank credit approval
Vanilla European USD/CAD call and put options and zero-cost collars for predictable USD-to-CAD conversion of app-store streaming revenues
USD/CAD cross-currency swaps to match the currency profile of rolling production financing and distribution minimum-guarantee draws
Listed USD/CAD futures and options on the Bourse de Montreal (TMX) for exchange-cleared exposure without bilateral counterparty limits

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in non-convertible or restricted customer market currencies (e.g., INR, VND, IDR, TRY) to lock settlement values of emerging-market subscription receipts without violating local currency controls
Natural hedging through USD-denominated operational accounts and USD invoicing of all foreign distribution contracts, reducing reliance on synthetic derivative positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA s. 252) - Corporations Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Notice of default issued by Corporations Canada; failure to file for two consecutive years empowers the Director to administratively dissolve the corporation (CBCA s. 212). A dissolved corporation loses legal capacity and may only be revived by Director's order or court application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including financial statements and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance of tax due 2 months after year-end (3 months for qualifying CCPCs under ITA s. 157(1.1))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per full month, capped at 12 months; repeated default increases penalty to 10% plus 2% per month, capped at 20 months; additional CRA penalty up to CAD 2,500 under ITA s. 162(7); daily interest; loss carry-backs disallowed until filing; arbitrary assessment under ITA s. 152(7).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and Comparative Financial Statements (CBCA s. 133(1), s. 155(1))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders (internal corporate action; resolutions must be recorded in the Minute Book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter interval between AGMs must not exceed 15 months; unanimous written resolution in lieu of AGM permitted under s. 142.1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court may order compliance under CBCA s. 247; directors and officers may be liable on summary conviction to a fine up to CAD 5,000 and/or 6 months' imprisonment under CBCA s. 250 for contravention; repeated default impairs corporate record continuity and due diligence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individuals with Significant Control (ISC / UBO) Register maintenance and annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (information submitted with the annual return); ISC Register must be available at the registered office for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register created within 15 days of incorporation; updates recorded within 15 days of any change, including shareholding transfers; ISC details confirmed with each annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under CBCA s. 21.4: on summary conviction, corporation liable to fine up to CAD 200,000 and responsible persons to imprisonment up to 6 months; court may order rectification under CBCA s. 247.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Extra-provincial annual registrations (licence of extra-provincial corporation) in each province where the entity carries on business - representative average fee; province-specific
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Applicable provincial/territorial corporate registries (e.g., Ontario Companies and Personal Property Security Branch; British Columbia Corporate Registry; Quebec Registraire des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Varies by province; generally within 60 days of the anniversary of the extra-provincial licence or on each annual anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, licence cancellation and loss of standing to enforce contracts in the province; continued unlicensed carrying-on of business is an offence under provincial laws.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold mandates an audit for a private non-distributing CBCA corporation; shareholders may annually dispense with an auditor by unanimous written resolution (CBCA s. 163). Distributing (public) corporations cannot dispense and must appoint an auditor and audit committee.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is the applicable framework for this private micro-drama corporation; comparative financial statements must be prepared for the AGM; CRA minimum record retention is 6 years (ITA s. 230(4)).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CBCA s. 21.1 requires an ISC (Individual with Significant Control) register updated within 15 days of any shareholding change; each annual return confirms ISC data to Corporations Canada. Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members, and ISC status is re-verified at every transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute Book (minutes of meetings and resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 650 per annum (Canadian registered office and corporate agent service; CAD 350 - 900 equivalent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 12,000 per engagement (small-entity CBCA audit; avoidable via s. 163 unanimous shareholder dispensation)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 5-15% under most tax treaties; Interest: 25% statutory, typically reduced to 0% under bilateral tax treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 50,000 for local file (related party transactions); CAD 50,000,000 for master file (group revenue)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Limited applicability under Canadian law; relies on General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and Controlled Foreign Company (CFC) rules to address artificial arrangements lacking economic substance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Summary conviction: up to 2 years imprisonment and $100,000 fine; Indictable: up to 5 years imprisonment and $1,000,000 fine
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, restitution orders, and potential disqualification from corporate directorships

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Canadian corporation with no real business activities, employees, or assets in Canada
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to $100,000 per violation; director fines and imprisonment for willful non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors personally liable for unpaid taxes, penalties, and possible criminal charges

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain arm's length transfer pricing documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustments to income up to 10-50% of transfer pricing adjustment; penalties of $1,000 to $100,000 per transaction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for penalties and interest if they directed or acquiesced in the non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and report suspicious transactions or maintain proper KYC/AML records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to $100,000 for corporations; criminal penalties including imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for directors who fail to exercise due diligence, including fines and jail time
